pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which words signal a simile? (1 mark)
   A. but and or
   B. to and from
   C. is and are
   D. like and as

2. What is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. A comparison using like or as
   B. A long story
   C. A saying with no comparison
   D. A kind of song

3. Which sentence has the punctuation of a list correct? (1 mark)
   A. We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   B. We wore, hats scarves and coats.
   C. We wore hats scarves and coats.
   D. We wore hats scarves, and coats

4. Why should each step contain only one action? (1 mark)
   A. To confuse readers
   B. To make it longer
   C. So it is clear and easy to follow
   D. To use fewer words

5. Which sentence needs a verb to be complete: Always ______ your hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. soap
   C. wash
   D. hands

6. Which device is used mainly to take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Radio
   B. Clock
   C. Camera
   D. Torch

7. How should notes be written? (1 mark)
   A. As whole paragraphs
   B. As short phrases of key words
   C. As long sentences
   D. As drawings only

8. Which question word asks about a place? (1 mark)
   A. Where
   B. Who
   C. When
   D. Why

9. Which is a rude phrase? (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Please continue
   C. Shut up
   D. Pardon me

10. Why do we put ideas in order? (1 mark)
   A. So the reader can follow them
   B. To use more words
   C. To make the story shorter
   D. To confuse the reader

11. In a script dialogue, what comes straight after the speaker's name? (1 mark)
   A. A bracket
   B. A full stop
   C. A number
   D. A colon

12. Why is reading fluently important? (1 mark)
   A. It hides mistakes
   B. It makes the book smaller
   C. It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   D. It ends the lesson early

13. What is a receipt? (1 mark)
   A. A shop
   B. A paper that shows you paid
   C. A kind of coin
   D. A type of fruit

14. Which sentence gives information but not an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Bring the clothes.
   B. Stay indoors.
   C. Today the sky is cloudy.
   D. Close the window.

15. Which starting sentence would make a reader curious? (1 mark)
   A. Page one.
   B. One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   C. The end.
   D. Yes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. List the two verbs in the sentence: The teacher counted the votes and announced the winner. (2 marks)

17. Join with but: The trader was tired. He kept working. (3 marks)

18. Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion. (2 marks)

19. Find the rhyming words in: Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play. (2 marks)

20. List three steps for understanding a poem. (3 marks)

21. Give three tips for telling a story well. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — like and as
   Similes use like or as.

2. A — A comparison using like or as
   A simile compares two things using like or as.

3. A — We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   A comma follows each item except the last two, which are joined by and.

4. C — So it is clear and easy to follow
   One action per step is clear.

5. C — wash
   Wash is the action word that completes the sentence.

6. C — Camera
   A camera takes photos.

7. B — As short phrases of key words
   Notes are brief.

8. A — Where
   Where asks for the place.

9. C — Shut up
   Shut up is disrespectful.

10. A — So the reader can follow them
   Order makes writing clear.

11. D — A colon
   The name is followed by a colon.

12. C — It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   Fluent reading helps meaning.

13. B — A paper that shows you paid
   A receipt is proof of payment.

14. C — Today the sky is cloudy.
   It only tells about the weather.

15. B — One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   A specific opening makes the reader want to read on.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: counted, announced
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb. Teacher, votes and winner are nouns.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: The trader was tired, but he kept working.
   Working / marking points: One mark for but, one for the comma, one for correct order.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: cabbages, onions
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: day and play
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read it aloud more than once, find meanings of new words, say the message in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Start with a clear opening, tell events in order, speak clearly, look at the audience, end with what you learned.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.
